title: Initializer Git Object Identity
purpose: Defines the canonical Git object identity representation used by every initializer record, eliminating independent and contradictory revision-string rules.

normative_requirements.text: A Git object identity shall be a structured representation with exactly two fields: object_format and object_id.
The object_format field shall be a string whose value is one of: "sha1" or "sha256".
When object_format is "sha1", the object_id shall be exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
When object_format is "sha256", the object_id shall be exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

The object_format shall match the source repository's native object format: a SHA-256 repository shall not accept a SHA-1 object identity, and a SHA-1 repository shall not accept a SHA-256 object identity.
Abbreviated object IDs are forbidden: every object_id shall be the full required length for its declared format.
Named references (branch names, tag names, symbolic refs) are forbidden as object_id values.
The identified source revision shall resolve directly to a commit object, not to a blob, tree, or tag object that does not ultimately resolve to a commit.
Every record in the initializer that stores or transmits a revision reference shall use the canonical Git object identity representation and shall preserve the exact full object_id value.
